Chapter 7: Traits

All Actions have traits. Traits have their own rule interactions. Traits with no rule of their own (such as Divine) are used by other rules and features.

Area

These Actions have an Area (see Areas), and can have a Distance that says how far from you the area can be placed. They target every creature inside their area that they affect, and they ignore Senses: they target creatures you perceive as Obscured, Hidden or Unsensed, with no penalty for it, and light doesn't change their roll. You need Line of Effect to the Point of Origin to place the area, and Line of Effect and Cover are checked from the Point of Origin to each creature. A Line has no Distance: it always starts from your square.

Body, Mind, Appeal and Instinct

An Action with one of these traits rolls that Attribute Modifier. A Body Action rolls Body, and so on. Some effects care about them, for example "your Body Actions gain 1 Boon".

When an Action has more than one of these traits, you roll the one with the highest value. The Action still has all of them: Trip is a Body Action and an Instinct Action, whichever it rolls. If the Action has a Vs. entry that says "the one used to roll," that Attribute is also the Defense: if you roll Body, you roll against Body.

Fear

The Fear trait has no rules of its own. Other rules, Talents and Tags refer to it.

Firearm

Firearm Actions need a weapon with the Firearm property (see Properties), such as a pistol or a musket, and use its Range as their Distance. A Weapon Action without this trait gets it when you use such a weapon (so a Weapon Attack with a musket is a Firearm Action). The trait and the property have one name, as Melee and Ranged do. A Firearm is not a Projectile weapon: Projectile Actions can't use it.

Focus

These Actions require concentration. This is not a mechanic by itself, but some features affect your ability to concentrate.

Handle

To use an Action with the Handle trait, you must be able to use your hands (or similar appendages). You also need a hand free to make any Action with this trait. Releasing an object costs no AP (Release). One exception: stowing an object you hold, or swapping it for another you carry (Interact), needs no free hand: the hand that holds the object does it. With both hands full you can stow one weapon, or swap it for another.

Melee

These Actions need a melee weapon used in hand, and use its Range as their Distance. A Weapon Action without this trait gets it when you use a melee weapon in hand (see Weapon Actions and Your Weapon).

Move

A Move is an Action with the Move trait.

To use an Action with the Move trait, you must have a Speed of at least 1.

You can't end your movement in a square with another creature (no movement can: see Movement). A creature can allow you to pass through their squares. Otherwise, passing through the squares of an unwilling creature is Difficult Terrain.

Nonlethal

These Actions deal Nonlethal damage by default. A Nonlethal Action can deal Lethal damage by taking a Bane.

Power

These Actions roll your Power Modifier.

Projectile

Projectile Actions need a weapon with the Projectile property (see Properties), such as a bow or a crossbow, and use its Range as their Distance. A Weapon Action without this trait gets it when you use such a weapon (so a Weapon Attack with a crossbow is a Projectile Action). The trait and the property have one name, as Melee and Ranged do.

Ranged

These Actions target creatures from a distance. The Action's Distance can be written like a ranged weapon's Range: normal / far / maximum, with 1 Bane at far range and 2 at maximum. A single number is a normal range only. A [Ranged, Weapon] Action needs a ranged weapon, or a weapon with the Thrown property used thrown, and uses that weapon's Range as its Distance. A Weapon Action without this trait gets it when you use a ranged weapon or throw a Thrown weapon.

Save

A Save Action: its targets roll a Save instead of you rolling against their Defense. See Save Actions.

Self

An Action with the Self trait always targets you, the origin of the Action. An [Area] Action with Self is centered on you: you are the target of its Emanation.

Signature

These Actions roll your Signature Modifier: the higher of your Weapon Modifier and your Power Modifier, even when they also have the Weapon or Power trait. They keep their other traits: a [Signature, Weapon] Action still needs a weapon and gets every effect on [Weapon] Actions (see Rolls). Signature is used for a class's own Actions, such as the Paladin's Smite.

Split

A Split Action has two modes, Weapon and Power, and you choose one each time you use it. In that use, the Action takes the chosen mode's trait and is an Action of that mode for every rule: a Weapon Action in Weapon mode (it needs a weapon, takes Melee or Ranged from it, and uses its Range), and a Power Action in Power mode (no weapon). The card shows the two modes side by side; everything else (Frequency, target, trigger, Critical) is shared.

Strike

Strike is any Action that tries to hit a creature, such as an attack with a weapon or a spell. You can make at most 3 Strikes per turn.

Unfailing

When the roll of an Unfailing Action gets a Tier 1, that use doesn't count toward the Action's Frequency: you can use it again. You still spend its AP, and its Tier 1 still happens. An Encounter Action with Unfailing that gets a Tier 1 is still unspent this encounter.

Weapon

This uses a weapon you are wielding. Actions with this trait require a weapon, and their Distance is the weapon's Range unless they say otherwise.

These Actions roll your Weapon Modifier. A Weapon roll normally targets Armor. When a rule calls for a Weapon roll against a DC, use the DC instead.

A Weapon Action with the Melee or Ranged trait needs a weapon with that property. A Weapon Action without them gets the one that matches the weapon you use.

Tags

Creatures have Tags instead of traits: words that other rules refer to, such as Profane (the Paladin's Smite). A creature's Tags are listed in its stat block. Like traits with no rule of their own, a Tag does nothing by itself.

To be decided

The list of Tags (Profane, Beast, Undead...) and what each one covers is not written yet.

Chapter 8: Conditions

These conditions are in alphabetical order. Unless a card says otherwise, a creature can't have the same condition twice: if they would gain a condition they already have, keep the longer duration, and for a condition with a value, such as Vulnerable 3, the highest value (see Stacking). A condition with a source, such as Frightened of a creature, Taunted by one or Grabbed by one, comes from one source at a time: if you gain it from a different source, the new one replaces the old one, with its own duration. The effect that gives a condition says how long it lasts (EoT, a number of rounds, until a Save: see Effect Timing); a condition written with no duration lasts until the end of the encounter. Ignoring a condition. A creature that ignores a condition keeps it, but the condition does nothing to it; its duration still runs, and it works again when the creature stops ignoring it. The conditions that come from damage (Bloodied, Strained, Desperate, Dying, Shattered and Unconscious) are in Health States.

Blinded

You can't see: for your Sight, everything is Darkness (see Senses). Creatures you only hear are Hidden to you, so your Actions against them are Doomed, and you can't target a creature you don't perceive. Any other Roll that needs sight is Doomed. Actions with the Area trait still affect the creatures in their area. Every square is Difficult Terrain for you, as Darkness is for a creature that can't see in it: you move by feel.

Dazed

Dazed always has a value, such as Dazed 1. When you become Dazed, you lose that many AP right away (never your Reaction AP). If you have fewer AP than the value, you lose the AP you have, and the rest is taken from the AP you regain at the start of your next turn; then Dazed ends. Dazed is the condition that takes AP now; Slowed takes them on your next turn.

Empowered

The first time you deal damage on each of your turns, add 1d6! to it (see Exploding Dice). The die deals the same kind of damage as the Action (its pool and its type). If the Action damages several creatures, you choose which one takes it. Empowered has no value: you are Empowered or you aren't, and being Empowered twice changes nothing.

To be decided

The die grows at later Stages (with those Stages' numbers).

Exhausted

Exhausted always has a value, such as Exhausted 2. While you are Exhausted:

  • Your Speed is reduced by the value (to a minimum of 1).
  • All your Rolls take a penalty equal to the value.
  • Your Resolve is reduced by 4 times the value.

A lower Resolve lowers your Health Pool, but not your Rally Points: they use your Health Pool as if you weren't Exhausted. The floor of a third doesn't apply to it.

If your Resolve reaches 0, you must make a Mind Save (DC 13). Resolve cannot go below 0.

Tier Result
Tier 1 You fall Unconscious and start a Sleep. You can't wake up while your Resolve is 0.
Tier 2 Your Exhausted value increases by 1, and you must make this Save again in 12 hours.
Tier 3 You must make this Save again in 12 hours.

Frightened

Frightened is always of a source: a creature or an object. While you perceive the source with your Sight (it is Clear or Obscured to you: see Senses), all your Rolls take 1 Bane, the Save that would end Frightened included, and every square that brings you closer to the source is Difficult Terrain for you (Forced Movement ignores it). Put a wall between you and the source, or let the source stand in Darkness, and it is out of your Sight: the Bane and the Difficult Terrain stop until you see it again.

Grabbed

A creature within its Reach holds you: you are Immobilized, and only the holder can Force Move or Reposition you (the holder's own Forced Movement or Reposition of you ignores your Immobilized). Grabbed ends when the holder lets go (no Action), when you are no longer within the holder's Reach, when the holder goes Down or is Unconscious, or when you end Immobilized with Break Free (1 AP [Move]). When the card that grabbed you says so, Break Free is a Body or Instinct Check (the higher) against the holder's Immobilized DC (see Immobilized). The holder can't use the hand or limb that holds you for anything else.

Half-Blinded

Your Sight perceives no creature better than Obscured: a creature that would be Clear to you is Obscured (see Senses). Your other senses aren't affected.

Hindered

Your Speed is halved, rounded down. If you become Hindered while you are moving, the movement you have left is halved too, rounded down.

Immobilized

You can't use Move Actions or Evade. If you become Immobilized while you are moving, your movement ends. Unless otherwise specified, you can remove Immobilized with Break Free (1 AP [Move]): the one Move Action you can use while Immobilized.

An Immobilized creature is also hard to move. An Action or effect that attempts to Force Move or Reposition you and doesn't roll is automatically disrupted: you aren't moved.

Example

Lana is Immobilized and her ally, Jared, has a feature that says "At the start of your turn, you can Reposition 3 an ally within Reach." If Jared attempts to use this on Lana, nothing happens and the effect is wasted.

If the Action rolls, the movement also needs the roll to beat the Immobilized DC: 11 + the Modifier the origin of the condition used (the Power Modifier for a Power Action, the Weapon Modifier for a Weapon Action, and so on; 13 if the condition has no origin; the highest if there are several). A Save Action doesn't roll, but it always has a Modifier: the origin rolls 2d12 + that Modifier against the Immobilized DC, once for all the Immobilized creatures it would move. If the result is below the Immobilized DC, you aren't moved. The rest of the Action works as usual. Steadiness applies after this check.

Imperiled

You barely avoided a Deadly Hazard: you are hanging from a ledge, balancing on the lip of a lava pit, or pinned at the edge of a crushing trap. While you are Imperiled:

  • All your Rolls are Doomed.
  • You are Vulnerable 3.

At the start of your turn you get back to safety, to a legal square next to the hazard, and stop being Imperiled. This takes no Action, but you are Slowed 1 that turn (or increase your Slowed value by 1), so no condition can keep you there. A creature can help you get to safety with the Interact Action (1 AP, Handle).

Lingering

Lingering X (Attributes) is damage that keeps coming: at the end of each of your turns, you take X damage, a number or dice rolled each time. It is Vigor damage when the Attributes are Bo/In and Resolve damage when they are Mi/Ap, unless the Lingering writes its pool before the value: Lingering [V] 1 (Ap) is Vigor damage with an Appeal Save. A Lingering can have a subtype, written after the value: Lingering [R] 1d6 Ho (Mi/Ap): a wound that bleeds, a fire that clings, holy light that keeps burning.

You can end it with the Shake Off Action (1 AP), on yourself or on a Lingering creature within your Reach: the Lingering creature makes a Save with the better of the two Attributes against DC 13, or the DC the Lingering writes (Lingering 1d6 (Bo/In; DC 15)). Tier 1: no effect. Tier 2: you take half the Lingering at the end of the current turn (even when it is another creature's turn, such as an ally's who used Shake Off on you), then it ends. Tier 3: it ends. Healing doesn't end a Lingering; the end of the encounter does. If you would gain Lingering again, keep the one with the higher average (see Stacking).

Pressed

Pressed always has a value, such as Pressed 1. Your [Strike] Actions take that many Pressure Banes (see Named Boons and Banes: at most 2 count). If you would be Pressed twice, only the highest value applies.

Prone

  • Melee Actions against you gain 1 Field Boon, and Ranged Actions against you suffer 1 Field Bane.
  • You can't Evade.
  • The only [Move] Actions you can use are Crawl, Stand and Break Free.

Quickened

Quickened always has a value, such as Quickened 2. You increase your maximum AP, and the AP you regain at the start of your turn, by the value: if you are Quickened 2, you regain 6 AP when your turn begins. You don't gain AP when you become Quickened, only when you regain AP at the start of your next turn. Quickened never changes your Reaction AP, and the extra AP you don't spend become Guard like any other (Unspent AP).

Sickened

Sickened always has a value, such as Sickened 1. Your Body and Instinct Saves take that many Banes, and you can't eat, drink or swallow anything: no potions.

Slowed

Slowed always has a value, such as Slowed 2. You decrease the AP you regain at the start of your turn by the value: if you are Slowed 2, you regain only 2 AP when your turn begins. You also reduce your maximum AP by the value. You don't lose AP when you become Slowed, only when you regain AP at the start of your next turn. Slowed never changes your Reaction AP: a Slowed creature still has its Reaction.

Slowed and Quickened cancel each other out, but they don't reduce each other's value: if you are Quickened 2 and Slowed 2, you regain the normal 4 AP. If one of them ends before your turn comes around (you lose Slowed 2 but are still Quickened 2), you regain 6 AP.

Staggered

You can't use Reactions. Your Reaction AP isn't lost: you can use it again when Staggered ends.

Taunted

Taunted is always by a creature. Your Actions against any creature other than it take 1 Bane.

Vulnerable

Vulnerable always has a value, such as Vulnerable 3. Actions against you gain a number of Boons equal to that value. If you would have Vulnerable twice, only the highest value applies.

Chapter 9: Glossary

Term Meaning
[Mod] Damage equal to the Modifier used on the roll: your Weapon Modifier on a Weapon roll, your Power Modifier on a Power roll, your Signature Modifier on a Signature roll, or your Attribute Modifier on an Attribute Action.
[W] The damage of your weapon, with the weapon's damage type.
[V], [R], [C] Vigor damage, Resolve damage, or the one the origin chooses. Vigor and Resolve are the thresholds of your Health Pool, not the Body and Mind Attributes.
[Trait] An Action with that trait: "a [Strike] Action". Several traits mean all of them: "[Ranged, Weapon] Actions".
0 AP An Action that costs no AP and can be used only on your turn.
0R A Reaction that costs no AP.
Action Points (AP) You regain 4 at the start of your turn, and 1 Reaction AP. The AP you don't spend stay for Reactions and give you Guard.
Advance Normal movement, up to the given distance, in one piece: the movement left is lost; one Interact can fit inside the Advance Action.
Ally A creature on your side. You are never your own ally.
Apex A class's big Encounter Action that needs Escalation 6; you choose one at level 4.
Area Where an Action's effect goes, written on its own line (with a Distance line when the area can be placed away from you). Those Actions have the Area trait: they target everyone they affect, ignoring Senses.
Armor Armor Defense (AD) — 11 + Armor value + other items + bonuses − penalties. The Defense against Weapon Actions.
Armor Training The heaviest armor a class can wear (it includes the lighter ones). Untrained: your Rolls are Doomed, Actions against your Armor or Ward are Favored.
Art A small class Action with three Modes; you take one at level 1 and a second at level 3.
At-will A Frequency: any number of uses, 1 Bane for each use after the first in a turn.
Attribute Action An Action that rolls the Attribute Modifier named by its Body, Mind, Appeal or Instinct trait (not a Weapon, Power or Signature roll).
Aura An area that follows its origin, written like Aura 2. You gain its effect when you enter it.
Bane, Boon Subtract or add 1 to a roll; they cancel each other. Named ones count up to 2 of each name. 5 or more left make the roll Favored (Boons) or Doomed (Banes) instead.
Barehanded A weapon property: it can't be disarmed and uses no hand, but needs a free hand.
Basic attack An NPC's main attack: 1 AP, At-will, Vs. AD or WD, with its rank's points an AP (see Points into damage: a flat number plus at most one small die, nothing added).
Blinded You can't see: heard creatures are Hidden to you (Doomed against them), sight Rolls are Doomed.
Bloodied, Strained You have Vigor damage at least equal to your Vigor (Bloodied), or Resolve damage at least equal to your Resolve (Strained). No effect by itself: Actions and features use them.
Body Action, Mind Action An Action with the Body or the Mind trait, even when it rolls another Attribute Modifier.
Breather 10 minutes of rest that removes all Nonlethal damage.
Buff An effect that modifies another Action, such as One More Arrow's 1[W] more on one of your [Strike] Actions.
Burst An area centered on a corner, where four squares meet: a 2 Burst affects every square whose center is within 2 squares of that corner.
Charge A Basic Action (2 AP, Round): Advance in a straight line at least 3 squares toward a creature, then make a Weapon Attack against it.
Check A roll of one Attribute Modifier against a DC (13 unless stated).
Class Actions The Actions your class gives you at level 1 (or a Hallmark Action: a choice of two).
Clear You perceive the creature well: no penalty either way.
Cleave Deal the Modifier used as damage to creatures next to the target.
Collision Where a Forced Movement stops when something blocks the destination the origin chose; the unused squares hurt.
Combat Value (CV) What an NPC counts for in an encounter: Minion 25, Grunt 50, Standard 100, Elite 200; less for an NPC of an earlier Stage than the party. CV 100 per PC is a normal fight.
Corners You can't cut a solid corner: anything solid, such as a wall, a pillar or an object that fills a square, that reaches the corner point where four squares meet.
Cover How well a target is protected: count the blocked corners of its space. 1 Field Bane for one, 2 for two; three make the roll Doomed.
Crawl A Move Action: you move 1 square (1 AP), or 3 squares (2 AP) when your Speed is 5 or higher. The movement a Prone creature can use.
Critical Doubles on a result that is already Tier 3, a total 20 or more above the DC, or three matching dice on a Favored roll. Only Actions with a Critical row use it; once an encounter, it also raises your Escalation by 1.
Daily Once per Sleep.
Dark Sight A Sight Sense: Dim light and Darkness count as Bright for you.
Dazed A condition with a value: you lose that many AP right away (never the Reaction AP); the rest, if any, from your next turn's AP.
Deadly Hazard A hazard that kills Minor enemies at once and leaves anyone else Imperiled.
Defense Armor Defense (11 + Armor value + items + bonuses − penalties), Ward Defense (11 + Power Modifier + Ward value + items + bonuses − penalties), or a Vs. Attribute (12 + the Attribute). "+1 Defense" raises all of them.
Desperate You are Down and still fighting (some Nonlethal damage, and a Nonlethal blow took you Down): Slowed 1, or your Slowed value + 1 (at most 3).
Difficult Terrain Each square counts double.
Dim-light Sight A Sight Sense: Dim light counts as Bright for you.
Disrupted A disrupted Action doesn't happen, and its AP and resources are wasted.
Distinct Choices A class's Attribute increases go to different Attributes.
Dominant Damage Whether you have more Vigor or Resolve damage.
Doomed A roll of 3d12, keeping the two lowest.
Doubles Both d12s match: the tier goes up.
Down Your total damage equals or goes above your Health Pool.
Dying Down with Vigor as your Dominant Damage: Slowed 1, or your Slowed value + 1 (at most 3); the first time in an encounter, roll on the Dying Table, then collapse or keep fighting.
Effect A card's line that happens whenever the card is used, whatever the roll.
Elevation Squares up or down count like a diagonal: the larger count plus half the smaller one. A creature is as tall as it is wide.
Elite An NPC rank with CV 200: about 130 Health at Stage 0, and the only NPC with Escalation (Elite Escalation: the 1-to-6 ladder, +1 a round and at each phase, with its own three steps at 2, 4 and 6).
Emanation An area around its target, a creature or a square: a 2 Emanation reaches 2 squares from it (the 1-2-1 shape; 21 squares).
Empowered The first time you deal damage on each of your turns, add 1d6! to it. No value.
Encounter A fight or similar scene, from Initiative until the GM ends it.
Engaged You are adjacent to an enemy and both of you can be Engaged, whatever you perceive. Other rules use it.
EoT Until the end of the turn of the affected creature.
Escalation A PC's adrenaline, a level from 1 to 6, never spent: 1 + the party's Momentum at the start of an encounter, +1 at the start of every round after the first, +1 once an encounter on a Critical and on your class's hook. Escalation Passives (at 2, 4 and 6) and the Apex work while it is high enough.
Escalation hook Your class's event that, once an encounter, raises your Escalation by 1 (the Paladin: an ally becomes Bloodied or goes Down; the Archer: an enemy you damaged goes Down).
Evade Movement that doesn't trigger reactions, in one piece.
Exhausted A condition with a value: less Speed, a penalty on all Rolls, a lower Resolve.
Exploding A die that shows its highest face and is rolled again: a d12 of a Roll counts the 12 as 11; a damage die written with ! (1d6!) counts its highest face as one less; every weapon's die is one.
Favored A roll of 3d12, keeping the two highest; any pair among the three is Doubles, three of a kind a Critical.
Field A named Boon or Bane from position and sight: Cover, Flanking, Prone, Obscured, Long, shooting into a melee. Up to 2.
Firearm A trait and a weapon property with one name: the weapon shoots with powder (a pistol, a musket), and a Firearm Action needs one. It is not Projectile.
Fists The Barehanded weapon every creature has (Melee, Non-threatening). While you have a free hand, it counts as a weapon you wield.
Flanking Creatures that threaten the same enemy: each gets 1 Field Boon on [Melee] Actions against it for each other flanker, minus 1 for each ally of the enemy that threatens it.
Forced Movement Movement you impose on another creature (Pushed, Pulled or Slid): no Reactions from movement, ignores Difficult Terrain, each square counts 1.
Frequency How often an Action can be used.
Frightened Of a source: 1 Bane on all your Rolls, and moving closer to it is Difficult Terrain, while you see it.
Grabbed Held by a creature within its Reach: Immobilized, and only the holder can move you; it ends when the holder lets go or you Break Free.
Grunt An NPC rank with CV 50 and 3 AP a turn: about 26 Health at Stage 0, dies to about 1 PC turn.
Guard A buffer written Guard N: it takes damage before your Health, doesn't stack (keep the higher) and ends with the encounter. Damage it takes isn't damage you take. The Guard of unspent AP adds to it and lasts 1 round.
Half-Blinded Your Sight perceives no creature better than Obscured.
Hallmark Action A choice of two class Actions at level 1; you take one.
Hallmark Reaction A choice of two class Reactions at level 1; you take one.
Hands Your main hand and your off hand, chosen when you make your character, and how many of them hold a weapon.
Hazardous Terrain [HT] Terrain that harms the creatures in it. Written [HT: Entering, Turn] in the text of the effect that creates it (notation, not a trait). It affects a creature at most once per turn-cycle.
Heal To remove damage. The creature chooses which damage.
Hearing A sense every creature has: you perceive creatures that make noise within 10 squares as Hidden, even through walls.
Hidden Your Actions against the creature are Doomed; its Actions against you are Favored when it perceives you better than you perceive it (two creatures Hidden to each other are both Doomed).
Hindered Your Speed is halved (after every other change to it).
Immobilized No Move Actions or Evade, and a movement you are making ends; Break Free (1 AP [Move]) ends it; Forced Movement without a roll fails on you.
Immune Damage of that subtype is 0 for you.
Imperiled Barely avoided a Deadly Hazard: all your Rolls are Doomed, Vulnerable 3, safe again at the start of your turn.
Initiative slot A position in the turn order.
Instance of damage One part of an Action's damage with its own pool and damage type; each [W] and each extra damage from another effect is its own instance.
Interact The Handle Action for objects and for helping others: draw, stow, swap, grab, open; help a creature stand up, get to safety or wake up. Once during an Advance Action, without ending it. Stowing or swapping needs no free hand (Handle).
Interrupt A Reaction that happens before the Action that triggers it.
Leaning Until the end of your turn: cover is calculated from one of your corners, and your own cover is reduced by 1 level.
Left your square Any change of your position, Forced Movement and Reposition included.
Lethal, Nonlethal The two kinds of damage. Damage is Lethal unless stated.
Light A weapon property: a small one-handed melee weapon (a Dagger, a Handaxe); 1 Bane in your off hand instead of 2.
Line An area that starts from your square, aimed at any square, written like Line 10: one square per step, the nearest to the segment; ties take one side, chosen before rolling.
Line of Effect A straight line from the center of your square to any corner of the creature's space that nothing blocks. Needed to target a creature, and for anything a card or a feature does to a creature.
Lingering Damage that comes back at the end of each of your turns (Vigor for Bo/In, Resolve for Mi/Ap); Shake Off (1 AP) and a Save against DC 13 end it; healing doesn't. Any damage type can linger.
Linked Action An Action another Action lets you use as part of it, written like Weapon Attack (1A). It costs no AP.
Long A weapon property: 1 Field Bane against adjacent creatures, and it doesn't threaten them.
Main hand, off hand Your two hands. [Strike, Weapon] Actions with a weapon in your off hand take 2 Banes (a Light weapon or your Fists: 1; a weapon held with both hands or a Strung weapon: none).
Mastery How well you know a kind of weapon: +1 with one weapon when your side wins an encounter that was normal or harder. Never lower than half your best in its group. 10 unlocks its Weapon Technique; 20, 30, 45 and 60 its later unlocks.
Minion An NPC rank with CV 25: about 12 Health at Stage 0, 3 AP a turn, no Reactions. Up to 3 Minions act in the same turn slot (the GM makes the squads: about one for every 2 Minions is recommended; the GM picks who goes next).
Minor enemies The Minion and Grunt ranks: 3 AP a turn, and their damage dice never explode.
Mode One of several things a card can do at the same cost; you choose one each time you use the card.
Momentum The party's number from 0 to 4: an encounter starts at Escalation 1 + Momentum. +1 for each encounter overcome; -1 when a PC goes Down and at each Sleep; lost on a retreat and at a Rest.
Move An Action with the Move trait.
Moved You moved with an Action that moves you, Evade included. Forced Movement, Reposition and Stand don't count.
Moves closer The distance between you is smaller after the movement; an Interrupt checks it square by square.
Moving away The distance between you is larger after the movement than before.
Named Boons and Banes Field, Pressure and Support: up to 2 Boons and 2 Banes of each name. Unnamed ones always add up.
Next Action An effect on your next Action with no duration must be used before the end of your turn, or it is wasted.
Non-threatening A weapon property: the weapon doesn't threaten, so you can't flank with it, unless a feature says otherwise. Fists have it.
Obscured Your Actions against the creature take 1 Field Bane; its Actions against you gain 1 Field Boon when it perceives you better than you perceive it.
Origin The creature that uses an Action, or the Point of Origin of an Area.
Pick One choice from a class's Repertoire; the level list says how many you take and from which list.
Point of Origin The place an area spreads from: an Emanation's target, your square for a Line, the tip of a cone. Line of Effect and Cover for the area are checked from it.
Power Modifier One of your class's two Modifier values (+2 or +1 at level 1; it grows at Stages 1 and 3). Power Actions roll it; Ward Defense adds it.
Power roll An Action with the Power trait (or a Split Action in Power mode).
Pressed A condition with a value: your [Strike] Actions take that many Pressure Banes (at most 2 count).
Pressure A named Bane an effect of another creature puts on you. Up to 2.
Projectile A trait and a weapon property with one name: the weapon shoots (a bow, a crossbow), and a Projectile Action needs one.
Prone A condition: Melee Actions against you gain 1 Field Boon and Ranged Actions against you take 1 Field Bane; you can't Evade, and your only [Move] Actions are Crawl, Stand and Break Free.
Properties The properties of a weapon (Actions have traits, creatures have Tags): Melee, Ranged, Light, Long, Projectile, Firearm, Strung, Thrown, Reload, Two-handed, Barehanded, Non-threatening.
Pulled Forced Movement toward the origin, up to its value, inside a 45° cone.
Pushed Forced Movement away from the origin, up to its value, inside a 45° cone.
Quickened A condition with a value: you regain (and can hold) that many more AP at the start of your turn; never more Reaction AP.
Rally Point Removes damage equal to a quarter of your Health Pool. Steel Yourself can't be used while Down or Unconscious.
Range How far a weapon reaches, melee weapons included: normal / far (1 Bane) / maximum (2 Banes).
Ranged Combat While Engaged Using a [Ranged] Action while Engaged: the roll is Doomed. Against a creature Engaged with someone else: 1 Field Bane.
Rank How much an NPC counts for in a fight: Minion, Grunt, Standard or Elite. It sets the NPC's CV, AP and the tables its ratings use.
Rating How strong one of an NPC's numbers is for its rank: Terrible, Low, Medium, High or Extreme (Minions have no Extreme). A GM can pick a number between two ratings.
Reach How far your body reaches: 1 square for every Species. Weapons have a Range instead.
Reaction An Action used in response to an Interrupt or a Trigger, with a cost like 1R (0R costs no AP). No creature has one by default.
Reaction AP The 1 AP you gain at the start of your turn that pays only for Reactions. It never becomes Guard.
Recovery The three ways to recover: a Breather, a Sleep and a Rest.
Regrip The Basic Action (1 AP, no Handle) to hold a weapon with both hands again, move it to the other hand or swap the weapons in your hands.
Release 0 AP: drop an object, or let go of it with one hand.
Reload A weapon property: a Reload Shot needs a reload afterwards.
Reload Shot A Favored and Empowered shot with a Reload weapon.
Repertoire Everything a class offers beyond its Class Actions, listed by Frequency: Passive, Turn, Round, Encounter, Daily.
Reposition Moving a creature along a path you choose, up to its value. Not Forced Movement: it never passes through creatures, never enters hazards, and needs Line of Effect.
Requirements What you need to use an Action.
Resist Resist N (subtype): each Action's damage of that subtype, both pools together, is reduced by N once (minimum 0).
Resolve, Vigor The two thresholds of your Health Pool: your class's high and low Health values (you choose which is which), your species' bonuses, and the Stage steps.
Rest A day in a safe place. It includes a Sleep.
Rider What follows the damage in a tier cell ("; Prone"): it happens on that Tier whatever damage is dealt (Resist, Immune, a reduction or Guard don't stop it).
Role What an NPC does in a fight (Striker, Soldier, Skirmisher, Artillery, Controller, Leader): a ready set of ratings, with no rules of its own.
Roll Anything you roll: a Check, a Save, a Weapon, Power or Signature roll, or an Attribute Action.
Round One full cycle of turns.
Save A roll a creature makes against an effect; its three values are for Tier 1 / 2 / 3.
Save Action An Action with the Save trait: its targets roll the named Save against 11 + your Modifier; Tier 1 is the worst for them.
Sense A way to perceive creatures: Sight, Hearing, Heatsight... Your best sense decides if a creature is Clear, Obscured, Hidden or Unsensed to you.
Setup What an Action does before the rest of it; optional unless it says you must.
Several Targets One roll for every target of an Action, each calculated separately.
Shake Off The Basic Action (1 AP, Handle) that ends Lingering: on yourself or a Lingering creature within your Reach, it makes a Save.
Shattered Down with Resolve as your Dominant Damage: Slowed 1, or your Slowed value + 1 (at most 3); the first time in an encounter, roll on the Shattered Table, then give up or keep fighting.
Sickened A condition with a value: that many Banes on your Body and Instinct Saves, and you can't swallow anything.
Signature Modifier The higher of your Weapon Modifier and Power Modifier. Signature Actions roll it.
Signature roll An Action with the Signature trait.
Size A creature's rank from 1 to 7, and how many squares it occupies.
Sleep 8 hours of non-strenuous activity, at most once every 16 hours; it renews Daily Actions.
Slid Forced Movement along a path the origin chooses (it can curve); the origin needs Line of Effect.
Slowed A condition with a value: you regain that many fewer AP at the start of your turn, and your maximum AP is that much lower; your Reaction AP doesn't change. Desperate, Dying and Shattered give Slowed 1 (or 1 more, to at most 3).
Special A card's line that is a rule about the card itself.
Special Action An NPC Action beyond its Basic attack: any AP cost and any Frequency, bought with the points of its rank's turn budget.
Specific beats general A card or feature that says something different from a general rule wins for that case.
Speed How far a creature can move with an Advance: species Speed plus class Speed Modifier.
Split A trait: the Action has a Weapon mode and a Power mode, and you choose one each time you use it.
Squeezing Moving through a gap one square narrower than you: Difficult Terrain, and Doomed and Vulnerable if you stop there.
SR Size Rank: a creature's Size as a number from 1 (Tiny) to 7 (Titanic). Medium is SR 3.
Stacking Bonuses don't add up: for each value (Guard included) use the highest bonus and the highest penalty. "Increase by N", Boons and Banes (up to the limit of their name), named bonuses (Field, Pressure, Support: different names add, the same name keeps the highest), Slowed increases and the Guard of unspent AP do add up.
Stage A group of levels: Stage 0 is levels 1-3, Stage 1 levels 4-7, Stage 2 levels 8-11, Stage 3 levels 12-15. Your numbers change only at a new Stage (Modifiers, Health, Guard per unspent AP, Rally Points; never your Attributes), and it sets the Bestiary's tables.
Stage Talent The Talent of levels 4, 8 and 12, the first level of Stages 1, 2 and 3.
Staggered You can't use Reactions; your Reaction AP waits.
Standard An NPC rank with CV 100: about 60 Health at Stage 0, dies to about 2 to 3 PC turns.
Start of the encounter After Initiative and before the first turn: abilities that happen then resolve one at a time, in turn order, which the GM can change.
Steadiness A creature's resistance to being moved: it reduces the value of Forced Movement and Reposition. Normally 0.
Steel Yourself The Basic Action that uses your Rally Points.
Strike An Action that tries to hit a creature. At most 3 per turn.
Strung A weapon property of bows: held in one hand and drawn with the other; 3 Banes on its Strikes while your other hand holds something.
Success A Tier 2 or 3 result.
Support A named Boon an effect gives several allies at once. Up to 2.
Swap squares Two creatures each enter the square the other left; a Reposition for each.
Tag A word on a creature (not an Action) that other rules refer to, such as Profane.
Taunted By a creature: 1 Bane on your Actions against anyone else.
Threatens A creature threatens every enemy within the normal range of a Melee weapon, for as long as it qualifies to use that weapon's Weapon Attack (1A); a Non-threatening weapon doesn't (not adjacent ones with a Long weapon).
Thrown A weapon property: the weapon can be used in hand or thrown, with a Range for each. A thrown weapon stays in your hand for the rules: the game doesn't track where it lands.
Tier The outcome of a roll: 1, 2 or 3.
Trigger A Reaction that happens after the Action that triggers it.
Triggering creature The creature whose Action sets a Reaction off.
Turn The time one creature acts.
Turn A Frequency: once per turn, on your turn and on each other creature's turn.
Turn budget The points of an NPC's whole turn, by rank and damage rating (a Medium Standard: 100, 25 points an AP), spent on its Actions: damage, riders, help, a Reaction.
Turn-cycle From the start of a creature's turn to the start of its next turn. A Round Action is used once per turn-cycle.
Unconscious You can't take Actions, you are Prone, and you drop everything you hold.
Unfailing A trait: when its roll gets a Tier 1, that use doesn't count toward the Action's Frequency. You still spend its AP.
Unsensed You can't target the creature; its Actions against you are Favored.
Version The same Action at another cost.
Vs. An entry that names an Attribute: the Action rolls against 12 + that Attribute of the target instead of Armor Defense or Ward Defense.
Vulnerable A condition with a value: Actions against you gain that many Boons.
Ward Ward Defense (WD) — 11 + Power Modifier + Ward value + other items + bonuses − penalties. The Defense against Power Actions.
Weak Weak N (subtype): each Action's damage of that subtype, both pools together, is increased by N once.
Weapon DC, Power DC The DC of your [Save] Action: 11 + the Modifier its other traits name (Weapon, Power or Signature).
Weapon Group Swords, Daggers, Axes, Hammers, Polearms, Bows, Crossbows, Firearms, Unarmed. Your Mastery with a weapon is never lower than half your best in its group.
Weapon Modifier One of your class's two Modifier values (+2 or +1 at level 1; it grows at Stages 1 and 3). Weapon Actions roll it.
Weapon roll An Action with the Weapon trait (or a Split Action in Weapon mode).
Weapon Technique A weapon's own Action, unlocked with Mastery; used only with that weapon, while you wield it.
Willing, Unwilling Willing: a creature that accepts the effect (an Unconscious creature counts as willing). Unwilling: one that doesn't.
Wound A result of the Dying or Shattered Table (Body or Mind).
Appendix

Appendix: Open Items

Rules that are not decided or not written yet. They are collected from the "To be decided" boxes in the chapters.

  1. Flying: Flying isn't written yet: going up and down, ending a turn in the air, falling when knocked Prone or Immobilized. Until it is, a creature that flies hovers just above the ground: it moves as on the ground, and the GM rules where flying matters.
  2. Line of Effect: Targeting walls and objects (and the Breach trait, to hit a creature behind a wall you break) is not written yet.
  3. Other areas: Cones are not written yet (and Lines wider than 1 square).
  4. Senses: Hiding and sneaking are not written yet.
  5. Wounds and the Tables: The entries of the Dying and Shattered Tables are placeholders.
  6. Talents: The Talents are set aside for now: none is in the book while the first three levels of the classes are finished. Every Talent slot stays empty until they are written again (the Skill Talents come with the Skills rules).
  7. Stages: Only Stage 0 is written so far: the classes' levels 4 and above, their Health steps for Stages 1, 2 and 3, and the Bestiary's later tables come after it.
  8. Tags: The list of Tags (Profane, Beast, Undead...) and what each one covers is not written yet.
  9. Empowered: The die grows at later Stages (with those Stages' numbers).
